paragraphs: ES&S has supplied election systems since 1979, describing them as secure, accessible and accurate. By its own account the systems are paper based, certified and fully auditable. They are sold to jurisdictions large and small.

The catalog includes ballot marking devices and tabulators. The DS950 handles Election Day, absentee and early vote ballots. On the ExpressVote, voters insert a card to activate the voting session, and the ballot is then dispensed for voter review. That device supports any language in audio and more than 30 languages in text. The ExpressVote XL displays the full ballot on a 32-inch interactive screen and produces an independent voter-verifiable paper record. Paired with an electronic pollbook, a polling place can check in voters and serve up to 15,000 different ballot styles. The ExpressVote 3 uses Secure Boot and application allowlisting to verify that only the certified operating system, software and firmware are on the unit.

ES&S says it has 31 voting systems certified by the U.S. Election Assistance Commission. It describes partnering with the Department of Homeland Security on industry practices. The company presents itself as part of the American Council for Election Technology. Its latest average rating by customers on overall satisfaction is given as 4.63 out of 5.

quote.text: America’s elections are a shared responsibility.
